answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small deposit that stays locked while it participates, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. Picture each verified agent as a raven tending its own garden plot on a shared island: the plot only yields rewards after sustained, useful work is attested by peers, and misbehavior forfeits the stake. Attackers pay a real cost per identity, while honest agents earn their deposit back through genuine contributions.
